description:

Replaces task-e6ed8bf1 (mangled title, archived). Fourth missing fact at the landed approval.decide_intent seam (approval-intent.ts:194-197, APPROVAL_MISSING_FACT_CODES[3] = APPROVAL_INTENT_BUDGET_REF_UNAVAILABLE @ DAEMON_APPROVAL_INTENT).

THE ORDERING PROBLEM, MEASURED AT HEAD 24ac4ae9: `ApprovalDecisionRecord.budgetRef` is required (packages/core/src/policy/approval-contract.ts:49; roster approval-validation.ts:25/:33, validHex64). The budget root digest is minted AT ACTIVATION: approval-activation.ts:116 `budgetRootFor` -> `resolveApprovalBudgetRoot(store, GenesisLegInput{ approvedRun{runBinding, verifiedGraphRevisionRef}, context{commandId, correlationId, decidedAt, principalId}, goalRef, projectId })` (budget/budget-genesis-leg.ts:185) -> `buildGenesisBudgetLeg` (:88) -> `authorizeBudgetRoot(store, {amounts: GENESIS_AMOUNTS, context, goalRef, projectId}, commit, genesisBudgetBindingPort(approvedRun))`, whose `digest` is "the writer's OWN canonical digest over the record it would commit" (:70); :168-170 refuses BOOTSTRAP_BUDGET_HASH_MISMATCH @ DAEMON_PREREQUISITE when a caller's claimed budgetHash disagrees; :176 persists it; graph-activation-service.ts:128/:181-192 mirrors it. The material includes the ACTIVATION envelope (context), which does not exist at decide time.

DELIVER (A): at decide time the record's `budgetRef` is a COMMITMENT digest over the budget material visible then — goalRef, projectId, approvedRun (runBinding, verifiedGraphRevisionRef), GENESIS_AMOUNTS and the store-read goal budget identity — EVERYTHING EXCEPT the activation context; at activation the same commitment is recomputed from activation's own reads and a mismatch REFUSES (exact code+layer, BOOTSTRAP_BUDGET_HASH_MISMATCH family) before the root is minted; the root digest is then minted as today. Ruling conditions, DoD-grade: (1) ONE shared canonical material builder feeds both the commitment and resolveApprovalBudgetRoot's record material; (2) consumer re-measure — graph-supersede-approval-binding.ts:73 (`record.budgetRef !== predecessor.boundHashes?.budgetHash`, a DIGEST comparison), expansion-approval.ts:227 / expansion-preparation.ts:83/:140/:242 (criteria.budgetRef), control-room approval-detail-plan.tsx:59, demo seeds; (3) bind-back refusal arm + one-field drill.

THE ARMS, each titled by the ONE mechanism that reds it:
- A DETERMINISM: two builds on one store are deep-equal and frozen, the digest is 64-hex and identical across both, and the material's shape is pinned field by field (projectId, goalRef, binding.graphRevisionRef from the verified run, amounts === GENESIS_AMOUNTS).
- B ONE FIELD, ONE DIGEST: a NAMED roster of nine mutations — projectId, goalRef, all six binding fields, one amount — each asserted to move the digest, with `toHaveLength(9)` as the denominator so a sweep that silently produced zero cases cannot pass. It ALSO asserts the nine resulting digests are mutually distinct: a digest that moved for every input but collapsed two of them would satisfy the loop while losing a fact.
- C DOMAIN SEPARATION, two inequalities rather than one. Not the untagged `sha256(JSON.stringify(material))`, so some domain/canonicalisation provably applies; and NOT the genesis ROOT digest for the same store. That second one matters most: the commitment and the root are different notions, and aliasing them would make the whole bind-back check vacuous.
- D ONE SHARED BUILDER — ruling condition 1, and the arm that makes it real. It compares two PRODUCTION surfaces to EACH OTHER: `resolveApprovalBudgetRoot(...).record.binding` must deep-equal the commitment material's binding, and `record.authorization.amounts` must equal its amounts. Comparing each side to a literal instead would let both drift together, which is precisely the digest-mirror failure the ruling names. Red until step 3 wires the shared port.
- E ABSENCE REFUSES: an unseeded goal yields the module's own `BUDGET_COMMITMENT_MATERIAL_UNAVAILABLE` at `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE` with the reader's own code carried as a non-empty upstream — never a zero digest. Collapsing the upstream would make "no such goal" indistinguishable from "the durable history is unreadable", which is the distinction budget-genesis-binding.ts exists to preserve.
- F BIND-BACK: the matching digest answers `{ ok: true }`; a different 64-hex answers `BOOTSTRAP_BUDGET_COMMITMENT_MISMATCH`; a NON-HEX ref answers `BUDGET_COMMITMENT_REF_MALFORMED`. The third case is deliberate — an arm that only checked "it refused" could not tell a caller who sent garbage from one who sent a stale digest.
- Plus a roster arm: frozen, duplicate-free, and containing all three codes.
Every expected code and the layer are TEST-SIDE literals; nothing is imported from the module under test to be compared against itself.

Exports BUDGET_COMMITMENT_LAYER, BUDGET_COMMITMENT_CODES (3, frozen), BUDGET_COMMITMENT_MATERIAL_KEYS, GENESIS_AMOUNTS, budgetCommitmentMaterial, budgetCommitmentDigest, verifyBudgetCommitment. The digest is sha256 over the domain tag `moe/budget/commitment/v1` + NUL + canonical text with sorted keys at every depth, keyed in BUDGET_COMMITMENT_MATERIAL_KEYS order.

CONDITION 1 IS WIRED, AND I HAD TO RESOLVE A CYCLE TO DO IT HONESTLY. The step says the leg should call `budgetCommitmentMaterial` while the commitment consumes `GENESIS_AMOUNTS` from the leg — that is a module cycle, and since `GENESIS_AMOUNTS` is a module-eval-time const it would sit in TDZ depending on which side loads first. Rather than paper over it, I moved the constant to the BUILDER, which is where condition 1 says the single source belongs, and the leg now does `export { GENESIS_AMOUNTS } from "./budget-commitment.js"`. Existing importers keep the name and the path; the dependency is one-directional (leg -> commitment); there is no second declaration anywhere. `buildGenesisBudgetLeg` now obtains the material FIRST and hands `authorizeBudgetRoot` both `material.amounts` and a binding port that returns `material.binding` — so the ledger record's binding and authorization ARE the builder's own objects, which is what arm D asserts between the two production surfaces.

ONE DESIGN CORRECTION TO THE STEP, because following it literally would have destroyed provenance. The step's refusal shape gives the caller only `upstream: {code, layer}`. The genesis leg must forward the binding reader's refusal in the READER's vocabulary, and that refusal also carries `sourceCode`/`sourceLayer` — which is precisely what tells a clean empty project apart from an unreadable durable history, the distinction budget-genesis-binding.ts exists to preserve (its own header says admitting the wrapper alone "would silently bootstrap over corruption"). Reconstructing a refusal from `upstream` would have dropped both fields. So the not-ok branch now also carries `refusal`, the reader's own object, and the leg re-raises THAT whole. `upstream` is kept for callers that only need the pair. The pre-existing budget-genesis-leg suite passing unchanged is the evidence this preserved behaviour rather than altered it.
